review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the definitions of simplePosSubgroup, simpleNegSubgroup, sl2RootX and sl2RootY. The only repeated proofs are short X/Y mirror pairs, and none is large enough to justify a shared lemma under the rubric. Those pairs are adjX_injective/adjY_injective, sl2RootX_rankOneRep/sl2RootY_rankOneRep, and the two map_one' proofs in the δ and ε constructions. Each is about 4–8 lines of routine unfolding, ext or rintro steps. A helper would need generic hypotheses over the X and Y families, so it would add API without removing real reasoning. The chains of `.trans` in eq_of_cartan_edges repeat across the E-type cases, but each case is a different diagram. That is a case enumeration, not repeated proof machinery across two proofs. The remaining proofs share no nontrivial argument. I did not run Lean, so I did not test any alternative.
